characters.name: Detective Dan Stark
characters.description: Beware the Silly Ones:Nostalgia Filterbuffoon and leech or not, he can dominate most gunfights. Brilliant, but Lazy: Dan has showed he is quite the competent cop and usually plays up hisObfuscating Stupidityto get close to a suspect, but he would rather do police work the way he did in the 80's rather than the more by the book way of the current time. Drunken Master: Dan can take on the world's second best assassin in a gunfight while heavily drunk. Which is handy, because he's heavily drunk at all times. Friend to All Children: Dan. He has kids doing exercises and pushups as part of a community outreach program, and they love him for it. They apparently join the police force at a rate that Lt. Ruiz can only describe as "Alarming." Jaded Washout: Several high profile failures and embodyingTechnologically Blind Eldersmake him stuck in property crimes well into middle age and he can resent it at time

characters.name: Detective Jack Bailey
characters.description: Badass in a Nice Suit: He dresses a lot better than Dan and gradually becomes his near equal in facing dangerous crooks Cloudcuckoolander's Minder: A lot of his average workday is correcting misconceptions Dan has or trying to downplay damaging statements Dan makes about how police work goes. Extreme Melee Revenge: After a hostage situation whereit is revealed that Jack's former partner is aDirty Copand took him hostageJack beats him while venting out his pent-up frustrations until Dan and Frank pull him off.Frankgives him one more kick while he's down. Friendless Background: His devotion to justice and being a cop as a kid made his classmates see him as a reviled tattletale and his closest academy peer bullied and cheated off him.

characters.name: Lt. Anna Ruiz
characters.description: Defrosting the Ice Queen: She always staysDa Chiefbut becomes gradually more willing to talk about a case or the detectives' social lives with then without permeating her every moment with distrust and contempt. Hidden Depths: She seems stern, humorless, andMarried to the Jobbut is in a yoga class and once made a sex tape with Dan before coming to hate him so much.

characters.name: Liz Traynor
characters.description: Hello, Attorney!: She is an assistant D.A. able to convincingly go undercover as a call girl. Reasonable Authority Figure: She won’t blanketly endorse Jack and Dan at their dumbest but does hear them out a lot more than their own boss and cooperate in information sharing.

characters.name: Julius Grant
characters.description: Character Development: He is initially justThe Stool Pigeonhelping Jack and Dan so he can stay out of jail while still committing crimes before gradually seeing them as more of friends and holding down honest jobs.

characters.name: Hodges
characters.description: The Millstone: Outside one tagger investigation, he is more likely to hinder a case than help it. He does show someBadass DriverCrouching Moron, Hidden Badasschops in "Vacation", but since he utilizes those chasing Jack and Dan as they're on the way to stop a prison break, it doesn't buy him any points. Thin-Skinned Bully: He is quick to rub in any humiliation Jack and Dan experience while getting bitter or meek when he gets mocked back.

characters.name: Samantha Evans
characters.description: 11th-Hour Ranger: She debuts in the last six episodes but is a determined and enthusiastic ally to the core cast. Part of it is being anIgnored Enamored Underlingto Jack, but there is also some genuine desire to make a difference and rapport with the cops. Genki Girl: Sam's habit of skipping around the Dallas PD and waving her arms around, not to mention her "getting into the moment" and greeting Liz like a best friend, definitely qualifies her as this. Jumped at the Call: She is quick to help out even with cases she wasn't assigned to. Nighmare Fetishist: She thinks fire crime scenes are cool. Smart People Wear Glasses: She is a techie and the only bespectacled characters m

characters.name: Pedro
characters.description: Always Second Best: He gets needled over only being the second-best assassin in the world and isn't crushed about having to kill the best one in a duel. Even Evil Has Standards: When Pedro has a gun to Jack's head, Jack states he is only interested in saving a female hostage that has nothing to do with this situation. After a brief pause Pedro not only allows him to live, but covers him as Jack makes his escape. Pedro later writes to him and tells him he admired his bravery and told his kids about him. From Camouflage to Criminal: He trained with the CIA before killing people freelance. Hitman with a Heart: He is an infamous killer who loves his family and can respect and spare aWorthy Opponent.

characters.name: Nigel
characters.description: Chronic Back Stabbing Disorder: He kills a guy transporting his goods for wanting a cut for setting up their warehouse even when the transport train got shut down, is planning to rob and kill the replacement transport guys rather than pay them and is enough of aCrazy Jealous Guyto try and shoot hisDirty Copaccomplice and girlfriend based on a near-stranger's claim that she has other boyfriends. He plays fair with his bodyguard but is also constantly insulting the guy's efforts to speak reason to him. Evil Brit: He's a snide, larcenous killer from England. Faux Affably Evil: He can sound quite sauve and fair for a few seconds at a time but is ruthless, petty, and condescending for the most part.

characters.name: Detective Kiersten Joyce
characters.description: Accidental Misnaming: Dan keeps calling her Kristen. So does Nigel, once. Dirty Cop: She handles big busts for the police…except when she helps her boyfriend Nigel escape their busts out of love and for a cut. Villain's Dying Grace: She ends up surviving and doing even more villainous stuff but does apologize to Jack when it looks like they’re both about to be executed because of her actions.

characters.name: Gemini
characters.description: Bad Boss: When one of his girls tries to quit, he holds her at gunpoint, takes all of her money, and burns all her stuff. Later, he throws the hotel manager working as the middleman between his girls and the johns off a roof the moment he gets mildly suspicious the guy talked to the cops and shoots his loyal bodyguard to sell aFaking the Deaddeception. Beauty Is Bad: He gets some shirtless scenes with aCarpet of Virilityand is one of the meaner episode main villains. Embarrassing Tattoo: He got a drunk tattoo of himself in a pimp pose with some girls and wants to get it removed. Faking the Dead: He kills his bodyguard and burns his house down to cover his escape from the country. The deception falls apart just five minutes later when Jack and Dan spot him at a pharmacy. Jerk with a Heart of Jerk: He briefly laments that he should have been content as an honest businessman like his father but is back to killing, threatening, and being a jerk before long.

characters.name: Steve Maxson
characters.description: Anti-Villain: He's a sad, frightened, previously law-abiding suburbanite whose plan is to neutralize criminal operations without hurting anyone. Dating What Daddy Hates: He feels as much emotion over his daughter dating a drummer as some men would if their daughters were dead. Deconstructed Character Archetype: He's less of a badassPapa WolfVigilante Manavenging his family like the Punisher than a meek chemist merely trying toHit Them in the Pocketbookand lacking the guts or the skills to do anything more serious than that. Inelegant Blubbering: He spends a lot of his interrogation crying unapologetically. Let Off by the Detective: Convinced that he's too soft for prison, Jack and Dan let him run and claim he overpowered them.

characters.name: Paco
characters.description: Bolivian Army Ending: He is last seen trying to convince some Mexican drug dealers that he didn't try to deliberately con them with a "Remember the Alamo" brick instead of a brick of heroin (Dan switched them) before they potentially kill him. Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: For all his cowardliness andKarmic Butt-Monkeymisfortune, he sets up his partner to be killed, and whenhegets double-crossed in turn, after initially crawling away in terror, he opens up on his betrayers with a machine gun and drives a burning truck after the cops who confiscated his drugs. Karmic Butt-Monkey: He is a drug dealing "weasel" and business partner keeps trying to kill him, Dan threatens him withCrippling Castration(it was aBrandishment Bluff) and then isMistaken for Racistand possibly executed by his new business partners.

characters.name: Eric Williams
characters.description: Big Brother Instinct: Inverted. He is implied to be the youngest of the three Williams Brothers, based on having the least authority, but he is willing to go on more than oneRoaring Rampage of Revengeover Russell's disappearance. Made of Iron: He is walking around fine during hisPerp Walkeven after being run over with a car. Not-So-Harmless Villain: His brother Keith poses the big danger for most of the episode, while Eric is more focused on the legitimate parts of the business and holding grudges over their brother, but he beats Keith unconscious, holds Liz and her mom hostage, and refuses to trade them for Jack (possibly preparing to kill them all) before his capture. Troubled Sympathetic Bigot:Played for Laughswith Eric, who believes his brother to have been killed by a Guatemalan gang, and burned the Guatemalan flag at his funeral, as well as smashing the windows of Guatemalan restaurants. He seems kind of chagrined in addition to being angry when he finds out that wasn't what really happened.

characters.name: Dolph
characters.description: Bad Boss: He murders a loyal and competent henchman who the police identified, is sending a whole crew of heisters to be killed or captured in a bank robbery that's really just a decoy for the real job, and gets angry and threatening to his real crew when they return without any money. Bald of Evil: His only hair is his beard, and he's aDiabolical Mastermind. Clock King: He times his men during robbery practice and is annoyed at anyone being even five minutes late for a meeting. Straight Edge Evil: He does yoga, won't eat meat, and he hates the idea of drug use but has no real apparent regard for anyone else. Taking You with Me: Even while suffering aprobably fatalheart attack, he still guns down several of his disgruntled partners.

characters.name: Bobby Kneecaps
characters.description: Face of a Thug: He looks and talks like he is mobbed up but is just a middle-class professional who has only ever been involved in two heists, to pay for his daughter’s operation and to repay a favor to the guy who gave him that plan. Let Off by the Detective: Dan lets him and his buddies go free in the end and pins their crimes on some less repentant crooks he'd just arrested for other, more serious crimes.

characters.name: The Drugstore Cowboys
characters.description: Beauty Is Bad: They are an attractive young couple wh are increasingly comfortable with violence, unlike middle-aged, out-of-shape Bobby Kneecaps. Even Evil Has Standards: Chaz dislikes the ides of hurting an old person in a robbery. Informed Flaw: Sid supposedly can't get pregnant because of how much she drinks and smokes, but she never does either onscreen. Lady Macbeth: Sid, the girl, is the mover and shaker of their criminal activities and dislikes signs sentiment and mercy. Lower-Class Lout: They are crooks who didn't graduate high school and can't afford a house or the clothes they want.

characters.name: The Duke
characters.description: Bald of Evil: He is a bald professional killer. Bunny-Ears Lawyer: The Duke, a hitman who lives in his mother's basement, is skilled enough to outwit and overpower two U.S. Marshalsand Dan. Crazy-Prepared: He keeps a paper clip hidden in his kitty and has trained himself to pick handcuffs with it. Creepy Monotone: He's a soft-voiced assassin who never changes his tone of voice except while calling out to his mother from a big distance. Even Bad Men Love Their Mamas: He's a feared assassin who still calls his mom.

characters.name: The Georgians
characters.description: Cold Ham: Nikolai is dour yet flowery in almost everything he says and does and rarely needs to raise his voice for it. Dumb Muscle: Nikolai and Buck are easy to defeat, but Sasha has a wrestler's physique and previously beat up about a dozen FBI agents with his bare hands and various loose pieces of furniture and lumber. He is also a grunting, antisocial type who kept getting forensic evidence all over himself at crime scenes and felt that wearing the hat of a man he killed and doing a shallow impression of him was the epitome of wit. Southern Gentleman: Buck is the most reasonable and polite of the trio, and is from Atlanta, Georgia, while Nikolai and Sasha come from the Democratic Republic of Georgia in the former Eastern Bloc. True Companions: Nikolai and Buck talk about Sasha, their muscle, as if he were a beloved pet or kid and feel miserable without him, wanting to break him out of prison after he chose toHold the Lineso they could escape a raid.

characters.name: Roland the Tech Bandit
characters.description: Consulting a Convicted Killer: Deconstructed. His skills at stealthy infiltration get him recruited to stop a hostage crisis and he is instrumental in saving the hostages but then promptly escapes despite having promised he wouldn't. Famed in Story: There is a documentary being made about a detective's long hunt for him. The detective eventually ends up being written out, with the film focusing solely on Roland. Graceful Loser: Long before the possibility of escape arises, he applauds his captors for their brilliance. Gentleman Thief: He is an eloquent cat burglar who steals to finance his passion of blogging about fine cuisine.

characters.name: Nate Bailey
characters.description: Evil Uncle: He got his own brother involved in a phony investment scheme decades ago, leading to the family losing their house and Jack's beloved dog, and while he seems eager to make amends and reform, he is using Jack and Dan to steal a bunch of the police's bait money and leaves behind a mocking note. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: He wears glasses, cons loved ones and sets up arson jobs.

characters.name: Perry
characters.description: Corrupt Bureaucrat: He takes bribes to make fake ID papers for criminals and make a guy seem eligible for retirement benefits in his thirties. Rail Enthusiast: He has model trains and pictures of trains in his house. Heel–Face Turn: Having to put up with his partner's unreasonable demands that could get them caught even as the guy wrecks his house and eats his food makes him almost happy to be arrested and agree to be in a sting operation. It's All About Me: He does have a lot to feel miserable about, but it's all he really talks about or notices.

characters.name: Kyle
characters.description: Badass Driver: When a hitwoman pulls a gun on him, he speeds toward her under fire and wrecks her car. Blue Blood: He has a ranch, went to Yale, and a big "family safe". Jumping Off the Slippery Slope: He starts out as just a corporate counsel who decides to sell information about a boss's wrongdoing to rival tycoons who will expose it without Kyle having to publicly do it himself (for free) and maybe get blacklisted. By the end of the episode, he's willing to try and offer to cover for the wrongdoers and let them kill Jack and Dan in exchange for his own life. Unseen No More: He is constantly mentioned but only seen in episode 16. Villain with Good Publicity: His whistleblowing is greedy and self-centered and he tries to sacrifice Jack and Dan's lives to save his, but he is seen as a popular hero by the police and media.

characters.name: Patrick Drayton
characters.description: Chekhov's Skill: Inverted with thelackof skill he displays playing golf. His lousy stance also causes him to be a poor shot with a gun in the climax. Corrupt Corporate Executive: He orders or personally commits multiple murders to suppress a report that he ignored safety and environmental impact reports for an oil drilling project. Jumping Off the Slippery Slope: He goes from being frightened and angry when his overzealous fixer kills one of the whistleblowers instead of just getting evidence from him to personally carrying out aSickbed Slayingof a second whistleblower the assassin failed to kill and then going after the third whistleblower and some cops at gunpoint. Snooty Sports: He's a smug, venal CEO who spends more time on the golf course than in his office.

characters.name: Angie
characters.description: Did Not Think This Through: She notes that becomingThe Mistressof a rich doctor and breaking up his marriage wasn't that smart when his wife was going to take half of their money. Femme Fatale: She seduces a doctor, is aMs. Red Inkmaxing out his credit cards, conspires with a fence side boyfriend to goad him into anInsurance Fraudscam so the could shake him down, then urges the doctor to kill the fence once he seems like a source of more money after all. She is also aHoney Trapto catch Dan for an attemptedOrgan Theft.
